title: Sell Mineral Rights in Avella, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Avella, PA | Cross Creek Area
metaDescription: Avella and Cross Creek area mineral owners: get a clear cash offer on your Marcellus interest, explained plainly, no obligation to sell.
heroLead: Out along Cross Creek near the West Virginia line, Avella families have watched drilling activity for close to two decades now, and plenty of them are still holding minerals nobody's explained clearly.
intro: Avella sits far enough west in Washington County that it borders West Virginia's own booming Marcellus and Utica counties, and a lot of the same operators lease on both sides of that state line. If your family farm straddled or sat near Cross Creek, there's a good chance your minerals have been part of a producing unit for years, and the royalty checks, however modest, have been arriving on a schedule you never quite learned to predict.

We grew up around this same kind of family land ourselves, and we know the frustration of a statement that changes every quarter without a clear reason why. That's exactly the gap we try to close before we ever put a number in front of you.

sections.heading: Wet gas, close to the border
paragraphs: This corner of Washington County produces some of the richest wet gas in the play, with a heavier natural gas liquids content than counties further east. That richness is good news for total value produced, but it also means a larger processing and fractionation step happens before your royalty is calculated, which shows up as a bigger deduction line on your statement than an owner further from the liquids-rich core might see.

Because Avella sits near the state line, some family tracts here were leased under older agreements written before the Marcellus boom fully took hold, meaning royalty terms and deduction language can look very different from a lease signed just a few years later.

sections.heading: The trip to the courthouse most owners skip
paragraphs: Washington County's Recorder of Deeds holds the chain of title that has to check out before any sale can close, and for family land near Avella that chain often runs through a farm deed from well before anyone thought about shale gas. We do that title work as part of preparing your offer instead of asking you to make the trip yourself.

sections.heading: Deciding whether to sell or hold
paragraphs: If your well is still early in its production life and prices are decent, holding may make sense. If your royalty has been declining for a few years, or you're an heir with a small fractional share and no real connection to the property, a sale converts that shrinking, unpredictable income into one settled number you control today.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Avella is close to West Virginia operators?
faqs.answer: Only in that some older cross-border leases have different terms than typical Pennsylvania Marcellus leases. We review your specific lease language before making an offer.

faqs.question: My royalty statement shows a big NGL deduction. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: In wet-gas areas like this one, yes, a larger deduction for gathering and fractionation of natural gas liquids is typical and legal under current Pennsylvania case law, even if it feels unfair.

faqs.question: How do you determine the offer amount?
faqs.answer: We look at your net mineral acreage, lease terms, unit production history, and recent royalty statements to build a number, then explain how we got there before you decide anything.
